applied.problem: The mistake "trusting a walk that swings either side of its steady line" is read alone for months; after i6 a lightly damped spring or circuit truly rings either side of its steady line, so the swing is only a warning sign when the rate depends only on the value.

"Where no formula exists" overstates the tank: dh/dt = 0.3 − 0.2 √h separates, giving time as a formula in the level; only the level against time has no tidy formula, as the next sentences rightly say.
"This rule has no tidy formula" is too broad: separating it gives time against level in closed form; what it lacks is a tidy formula for h against time, which is why no exact curve is drawn.
